## Introduction

Good analysis requires good data, but how can a high-quality AIRR dataset be
distinguished from a low-quality one? RepCred identifies and reports several key
metrics that can indicate potential problems in a repertoire. Modeled after
FastQC, it provides an easily digestible summary for novices and experts alike.

The only input required is a file describing IG and/or TCR rearrangements in the
[AIRR TSV format](https://docs.airr-community.org/en/stable/datarep/rearrangements.html).
Optionally, the germline reference set used for annotation (one or more FASTA files)
can be provided; gene and allele calls are then checked against it, and calls that
are absent from the reference are listed in the report.

The report contains:

- **Quality control stats**: AIRR compliance, and the percentage of rows with missing
  data in each column.
- **Non-nucleotides in sequence**: characters other than A, C, G, T in `sequence`.
- **Statistics**: productive vs. non-productive sequences, and sequence length
  distributions.
- **Annotation calls statistics**: number of unique allele calls per gene and relative
  gene usage.
- **General statistics**: hot/cold spot counts and GC content (requires
  `sequence_alignment`).
- **Possible chimerisms**: CDR3 sequences associated with more than one V gene.

By default, repertoires are randomly downsampled to 5000 rearrangements, with a
fixed seed so that the same input gives the same report. The number can be changed
(`downsample_n` in R, `-n` on the command line). The report lists the MD5 checksum
of the repertoire and germline files it was generated from.

RepCred is maintained by the
[Software Working Group](https://www.antibodysociety.org/the-airr-community/airr-working-groups/software/)
of the Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire Community (AIRR-C).

## Usage

There are several ways to generate the credibility report. All of them use the same
report template. The examples below use the small example repertoire included in the
package.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(repcred)
rep_file <- system.file("extdata", "ExampleDb.tsv", package = "repcred")
```

### R function

`repcred_report()` renders the report and returns the path to it. `format` is one of
`"html"`, `"pdf"` or `"all"`. Pass `downsample = FALSE` to analyse every rearrangement,
or `downsample_n` to change how many are kept (default 5000).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
report <- repcred_report(rep_file, outdir = "repcred-report", format = "html")
```

To check the calls against the germline reference used for annotation:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
report <- repcred_report(rep_file, outdir = "repcred-report",
                         genome_file = c("IGHV.fasta", "IGHD.fasta", "IGHJ.fasta"))
```

### Shiny app

`repcredWeb()` launches a web application where the repertoire (and, optionally,
germline reference files) can be uploaded and the report viewed and downloaded.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
repcredWeb()
```

### Command line

The script `repcred.R` is installed with the package:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
Rscript $(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("repcred.R", package="repcred"))') \
    -r ExampleDb.tsv -o repcred-report -f html
```

Options: `-r` repertoire file, `-o` output directory, `-f` format (`html`, `pdf`, `all`),
`-d` downsample (`TRUE`/`FALSE`), `-n` number of sequences to keep when downsampling
(default 5000), `-g` comma separated germline FASTA files.

The same command is available in the Docker image:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/home:z ghcr.io/airr-community/repcred:latest repcred -r ExampleDb.tsv -o repcred-report
```

### RStudio

To customise the report, create a project with the report template from RStudio:
*File > New Project > New Directory > AIRR-C: Repertoire Credibility Project*. The report is
`index.Rmd` and can be edited and rendered with bookdown.
